lines: * Exam for run-178 task 1 — "The boot asks Jev about every residual row, once,
* through the edge, and writes the answers beside its own kind" (#1093).
* CLAIM. Open a finished run's evidence tag and read `residuals.jsonl`: every
* row still carries the boot's own `kind`, and beside it a `jev` object with
* the classifier's status and subject, its actor, its attention score and its
* claim-falsity — or no `jev` at all on a row whose request failed, with one
* boot-log line saying so and the pull request exactly as it would have been.
* Six machine clauses, read here leg by leg and nowhere else. Every assertion
* names the leg it belongs to and the clause it comes from, so a reader can map
* this file back to the contract:
*       beside `KATA_URL`; every request to Jev is one `fleet_curl` whose argv
*       `Authorization`, `Bearer` or the API key's name, and the script's text
*       holds that name nowhere (`KEY_NAME` below)                  → leg (a)
*   M2  k checklist items, exactly k requests for the whole boot, one per item,
*       each one line of `residuals-jev.jsonl` — `{answers, error, key, model,
*       usage}`, the key the sha256 of `<name>\n<text>` — and no later
*       transition re-asks a key the file already carries               → leg (b)
*   M3  every row whose request succeeded carries, beside the rule's `kind`, a
*       `kind`, `model`, read off that row's own reply; `file`, `kind`, `line`,
*   M4  the request body: `state.task` off the plan (or `null`), `state.finding`
*       the row, `model` `jev-latest`, and a `questions` map of exactly the five
*       ids with exactly the criteria each one names                    → leg (d)
*   M5  a failing `fleet_curl` writes exactly one `jev: <name> — curl exit <n>`
*       line, leaves that row with NO `jev` key, and the boot publishes a body
*       byte-identical to the succeeding run's                          → leg (e)
*   M6  the rig's curl stub gains the `/v1/systemone` arm with its payload log,
*       its answers file, its single-reply knob and its exit knob; the README
*       names this sim; the edited script still parses                  → leg (f)
* FOUR BOOTS, NO MORE, over ONE fixture. A boot is ~40 forks of stub shell, so
* every leg that needs one shares these four; each is started once, eagerly, and
* awaited by everyone who reads it — the shape `test_sandbox_boot_amendments.mjs`
* uses for its two. The fixture is the one the task's Context pins: the rig's
* own `DEFAULT_REPORT` with a two-piece `notes` on its done task row, and a
* `PASS` receipt carrying one `deferred:external` ack — THREE checklist items,
*   SUCCEEDED  the stub answers every request with its default reply. Legs (a),
*   ALT_URL    the same boot with `FLEET_TYPESAFE_URL` pointing elsewhere, so
*              the stub's `*)` fallthrough answers UNKNOWN and the argv log is
*              the only thing the leg reads. Leg (a)'s second half.
*   CHOSEN     `STUB_TYPESAFE_ANSWERS` maps the needle `rename fold_now` to one
*              reply and `STUB_TYPESAFE_ANSWER` answers the other two, so one
*              boot exercises both knobs AND their precedence. Leg (c)'s second
*              half, and leg (f)'s reading of the arm.
* THE RECEIPT SAYS `PASS`. `do_boot` greens a run on `verdict = PASS`; a receipt
* spelling anything else parks it and its card opens `**Parked:**`. The ack
* rides on the rig's own default receipt plus the one `gateCheck.acks` entry.
* THE EXPECTATIONS ARE THE CLAUSE APPLIED TO THE FIXTURE. `jevOf(reply)` below
* is M3's own rule, so a row's expected `jev` is derived from the reply the stub
* was told to give and is not a second hand-written copy of it — except where
* the Proof leg spells a literal (`jev.kind`, `0.8`, `0.05`, the sha256 key,
* the three checklist lines), which is asserted as the literal it spells.
* TWO `Run:` LINES ARE READ HERE AS FILE READS. The Proof's first and second
* `Run:` lines — no API key name in the script, the `TYPESAFE_URL`
* definition verbatim — are the driver's to run, and leg (a) names them; the
* same two readings are made here directly off the script's text, which is the
* reading this file can make on its own.
* WHAT LEG (f) IS NOT. Its fourth `Run:` line runs a sibling sim. This file may
* not: `fleet/tests/test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs` M4 forbids a sim from spawning,
* or even checking the existence of, another sim, and a sim that broke that
* probe would cost the run more than the leg buys. So no sibling sim is named
* here at all. What is left is the reading this exam can make on its own: the
* arm exercised end to end by legs (b), (c) and (e) — payload log, answers file,
* single-reply knob, exit knob — the `CALL curl typesafe` line the arm's `say`
* writes, the README index line read with `fs`, and `bash -n` over the script
SCRIPT, ENV, BASE_SHA, DEFAULT_REPORT, RUN_PATH, PLAN_TASK_ID, PLAN_TASK_CLAIM,
argvLines, lines, prPosts, readLog, states, stream, runTests,
/** The checkout, from the script the rig points at — `fleet/sandbox-boot.sh`. */
* The Jev bearer key's environment-variable name — the one M1 says the script
* and its argv must never spell, because the edge injects the bearer the way it
* SPELLED IN PIECES ON PURPOSE. A repo-wide guard greps `fleet`, `skills`,
* `tests` and `hooks` for the key's name and expects no file to carry it; an
* exam that asserts the name's absence must not itself be the hit. Joining the
* three words here keeps the reading exactly what M1 words — the leg still
* compares against the real name — while leaving this file clean for the grep.
// ── the fixture: three items, three requests ─────────────────────────────────
/** The ack's detail, and the two `; `-separated pieces of the task's notes. */
const ACK_DETAIL = 'the deploy waits on a credential'
const UNVERIFIED_TEXT = 'could not verify the port is free at runtime'
* The three items in `residual_read`'s own order — the acks first, then the
* merged tasks' notes — each with the name it is checklisted under, the kind
* BASE's rule gives it and the task it belongs to.
{ name: ACK_NAME, text: ACK_DETAIL, kind: 'deferred', task: null },
{ name: REVIEWER_NAME, text: UNVERIFIED_TEXT, kind: 'unverified', task: PLAN_TASK_ID },
{ name: REVIEWER_NAME, text: NIT_TEXT, kind: 'nit', task: PLAN_TASK_ID },
/** The rig's own report, with the two-piece `notes` on its one done task. */
/** The rig's own `PASS` receipt, plus the one ack the checklist is read from. */
gateCheck: { acks: [{ type: ACK_NAME, detail: ACK_DETAIL }] },
* The key M2 spells: the sha256 hex of `<name>\n<text>`. The Context works one
* of the three out by hand, and leg (b) names it — `KEY_WORKED` below is that
* value, asserted against this function so the fixture and the clause agree
// ── the replies the stub is told to give ─────────────────────────────────────
* THE DEFAULT REPLY the arm emits when no knob names another — the Context's,
* verbatim, attention `0.8`, below the card's `2.5` threshold, so no sim that
* does not ask for one ever sees a card section.
* The reply the answers file maps the needle `rename fold_now` to: leg (c)'s
* `unverified` / `proof leg` / `examiner` / `2.9`. Every field differs from the
* default's, its model included, so a row that took the wrong reply — or that
* took one reply for every row — fails rather than passing by coincidence.
* The single-reply knob's answer, third and distinct again. It rides on the
* SAME boot as the answers file, which is what makes the precedence M6 spells —
* the file first, `STUB_TYPESAFE_ANSWER` second — readable in one run: the
* needle's row must take ALT and the other two must take this.
/** The needle the answers file keys ALT_REPLY on — a substring of one payload. */
* M3's own rule, applied to a reply: the `jev` object a row whose request
* answered with `reply` must carry. The expectation is the clause, not a second
/** M3's key list, in the order M3 gives it. */
/** The row's keys, in the order `sort_keys=True` puts them with `jev` present. */
/** M2's cache-line keys, in the order M2 gives them. */
* The credential name M1 says the boot must carry nowhere, spelled in two
* pieces so this file's own text does not hold it: the run's tree-wide
* `grep -rIl` reads any occurrence as a site that handles the key.
/** The production endpoint M1 pins, and the one the knob redirects to. */
/** One boot of the fixture, started once, its `ctx` resolved when it exits 0. */
// `<needle><TAB><reply JSON>`, one line, written under the case's own home.
// Every boot is started here, before the first case runs, so the four run
// beside each other rather than one after another.
/** Every curl argv of the run whose URL ends `/v1/systemone`. */
/** The payloads the stub logged, in the order it was called. */
/** The evidence branch's residual ledger for this run, raw and parsed. */
/** The per-request cache beside it, raw and parsed. */
/** The one row of a ledger whose `text` is `text`. */
assert.equal(rows.length, 1, `the ledger must hold exactly one row for ${JSON.stringify(text)}\n${ledgerRaw(ctx)}`)
/** The one PR body this run POSTed, whole. */
assert.equal(posts.length, 1, `the run opened ${posts.length} PRs, not one`)
/** The element of `argv` directly after the first `flag`, or undefined. */
/** Whether `flag` stands anywhere in `argv` with `value` directly after it —
*  "carries `-H` then `content-type: application/json`", which is what M1 asks
*  and which a second `-H` of another name does not disturb. */
argv.some((s, i) => s === flag && argv[i + 1] === value)
/** The script's own text — the two `Run:` readings leg (a) names. */
// ── leg (a) — M1: the constant, the argv, and no credential anywhere ─────────
test('(a) [M1] the script defines TYPESAFE_URL verbatim and names the API key nowhere', () => {
`(a) [M1] the script's text must contain the string \`${KEY_NAME}\` nowhere — the edge `
+ 'injects the bearer, exactly as it does for `claude-max` and `kata`',
'(a) [M1] the fixture no longer holds: `KATA_URL` is not defined the way this leg reads it beside',
test('(a) [M1] every request to Jev is one POST to the endpoint, carrying no credential', async () => {
`(a) [M1] a run whose checklist holds ${ITEMS.length} items must make ${ITEMS.length} requests `
`(a) [M1] the URL must be exactly \`${ENDPOINT}\` — https, and the one path: ${shown}`,
assert.ok(payload !== undefined, `(a) [M1] \`-d\` then the JSON body, inline and never \`@-\`: ${shown}`)
`(a) [M1] the argv word after \`-d\` must be a JSON body: ${shown}`,
`(a) [M1] no argv element may contain \`${forbidden}\` — the edge injects the bearer: ${shown}`,
test('(a) [M1] FLEET_TYPESAFE_URL moves every request, and nothing reaches the production host', async () => {
`(a) [M1] the redirected run must still make ${ITEMS.length} requests, one per item, `
'(a) [M1] with the knob set, no request may reach `typesafe.int.exe.xyz` at all — the literal is '
+ 'the default and not a second address the boot also tries',
// ── leg (b) — M2: one request per item, cached, never re-asked ───────────────
test('(b) [M2] the payload log holds one line per item, though evidence was collected more than once', async () => {
`(b) [M2] \`typesafe.log\` must hold exactly ${ITEMS.length} lines — one per checklist item for `
// The transitions that would each have re-asked, had the cache not held them.
`(b) [M2] the boot must have passed through \`${state}\` — the leg is about a SECOND `
`(b) [M2] \`collect_evidence\` must have run at least twice after the report existed, or the `
+ `count above proves nothing about a re-ask:\n${collections.join('\n')}`,
test('(b) [M2] the cache holds one line per request, keyed, with the answers and no error', async () => {
'(b) [M2] the fixture no longer agrees with the key the plan works out by hand',
`(b) [M2] a cache line's keys must be exactly ${JSON.stringify(CACHE_KEYS)}, in that order: `
assert.equal(row.error, null, `(b) [M2] a request that answered has \`error\` null: ${JSON.stringify(row)}`)
// One key per item, every one of them the sha256 M2 spells, and none twice.
`(b) [M2] the keys must be the sha256 hex of \`<name>\\n<text>\` for the three items\n${cacheRaw(ctx)}`,
`(b) [M2] no key may appear twice — a second transition re-asked one\n${cacheRaw(ctx)}`,
`(b) [M2] the \`${UNVERIFIED_TEXT}\` item's line must carry key \`${KEY_WORKED}\`\n${cacheRaw(ctx)}`,
// ── leg (c) — M3: the row, its kind, and the jev beside it ──────────────────
test('(c) [M3] every row carries BASE\'s own fields and a jev of exactly the six keys', async () => {
`(c) [M3] the ledger must hold exactly ${ITEMS.length} rows\n${ledgerRaw(ctx)}`,
`(c) [M3] a row's keys must be exactly ${JSON.stringify(ROW_KEYS)}, in that order: `
`(c) [M3] a \`jev\`'s keys must be exactly ${JSON.stringify(JEV_KEYS)}, in that order: `
// The literals the leg spells, one by one, and then the object whole.
assert.equal(row.jev.actor, 'nobody', `(c) [M3] \`jev.actor\` is the actor answer's choice: ${JSON.stringify(row.jev)}`)
`(c) [M3] \`jev.confidence\` is the three choice answers' confidences: ${JSON.stringify(row.jev)}`,
`(c) [M3] the whole \`jev\` is the reply read through M3's rule: ${JSON.stringify(row.jev)}`,
// BASE's own fields, unchanged by any of this.
assert.equal(row.file, null, `(c) [M3] no fixture text names a path, so \`file\` is null: ${JSON.stringify(row)}`)
assert.equal(row.run, 'run-7', `(c) [M3] \`run\` is the run id BASE writes: ${JSON.stringify(row)}`)
assert.equal(row.sha, BASE_SHA, `(c) [M3] \`sha\` is the base sha BASE writes: ${JSON.stringify(row)}`)
// The rule's own `kind` on each of the three, and the task each belongs to.
`(c) [M3] \`kind\` is still BASE's — \`unverified\` for a text containing \`could not verify\`, `
`(c) [M3] \`task\` is what BASE writes — the id for a reviewer piece, null for an ack: `
test('(c) [M3] the row the answers file names takes that reply, and no other row does', async () => {
assert.equal(rows.length, ITEMS.length, `(c) [M3] three rows here too\n${ledgerRaw(ctx)}`)
assert.ok(NIT_TEXT.includes(NEEDLE), '(c) [M3] the fixture\'s needle is no longer a substring of that text')
`(c) [M3] the row whose payload carries \`${NEEDLE}\` must carry THAT reply's answers — `
// Its own `kind` is untouched by what Jev said about it.
`(c) [M3] the rule's \`kind\` is the boot's own and never the classifier's: ${JSON.stringify(needled)}`,
// And no other row's. The other two answered with the single-reply knob, so
// "not the needle's" is proven by what they ARE, not merely by inequality.
`(c) [M3] a row whose payload does not carry the needle takes the single-reply answer, not the `
// ── leg (d) — M4: the body, the state, and the five questions ────────────────
test('(d) [M4] each payload is the row\'s state, the model, and exactly the five questions', async () => {
assert.equal(raw.length, ITEMS.length, `(d) [M4] one payload per item\n${raw.join('\n')}`)
// One payload per item, matched on the finding it carries.
`(d) [M4] \`state.finding.text\` is the row's text, one payload per row\n${raw.join('\n')}`,
assert.equal(doc.state.finding.file, null, `(d) [M4] \`state.finding.file\` is the row's file: ${shown}`)
assert.equal(doc.state.finding.line, null, `(d) [M4] \`state.finding.line\` is the row's line: ${shown}`)
`(d) [M4] \`questions\` must have exactly the five ids ${JSON.stringify(QUESTION_IDS)} — a `
+ `payload that folded status and subject into one question fails here: ${shown}`,
`(d) [M4] \`status\`'s criteria keys are exactly verified, unverified, deferred: ${shown}`,
`(d) [M4] \`subject\`'s criteria keys are exactly the six subjects: ${shown}`,
`(d) [M4] \`actor\`'s criteria keys are exactly implementer, plan, examiner, nobody: ${shown}`,
`(d) [M4] \`attention\`'s criteria is an ordered array of exactly four levels: ${shown}`,
// THE STATE'S `task`: the plan's own row for a reviewer piece, null for the
// ack, which no single task owns.
`(d) [M4] a row no single task owns sends \`state.task\` null: ${JSON.stringify(ackBody)}`,
assert.ok(task && typeof task === 'object', `(d) [M4] a reviewer piece sends its task's row: ${shown}`)
`(d) [M4] \`state.task\` is \`{title, claim, machine, files}\` read off the plan: ${shown}`,
task.title, 'The smoke target grows a file',
`(d) [M4] \`claim\` is the \`**Claim:**\` sentence with its provenance tag stripped: ${shown}`,
// ── leg (e) — M5: a failed request costs the row its jev and nothing else ────
test('(e) [M5] a failing curl writes one log line per item and leaves every row without a jev', async () => {
`(e) [M5] exactly one \`jev: <name> — curl exit <n>\` line per failed item — two naming `
assert.equal(rows.length, ITEMS.length, `(e) [M5] the ledger still holds three rows\n${ledgerRaw(ctx)}`)
`(e) [M5] a row whose request failed carries NO \`jev\` key — not a null one: ${JSON.stringify(row)}`,
`(e) [M5] and is otherwise the row BASE writes: ${JSON.stringify(row)}`,
`(e) [M5] the failed requests are cached too — that is what stops the next transition `
assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(row), CACHE_KEYS, `(e) [M5] the same five keys: ${JSON.stringify(row)}`)
assert.equal(row.usage, null, `(e) [M5] \`usage\` null — there was no reply: ${JSON.stringify(row)}`)
// The line belongs to a request that FAILED, and to no other: the run whose
// requests all answered writes none of it.
'(e) [M5] a run whose requests all answered writes no `curl exit` line at all — the line is '
test('(e) [M5] the failed run publishes the byte-identical body, and both render BASE\'s checklist', async () => {
'(e) [M5] a run whose every TypeSafe request failed must publish the same pull request body, '
+ 'byte for byte, as one whose requests all succeeded',
// And that body is BASE's rendering: the count, the errand, the section.
for (const [which, text] of [['the failed', badBody], ['the succeeding', goodBody]]) {
`(e) [M5] ${which} card must carry the ack's errand line\n${text}`,
assert.ok(at >= 0, `(e) [M5] ${which} card must carry a \`### Residuals\` section\n${text}`)
`(e) [M5] ${which} card's \`### Residuals\` section is BASE's three checklist lines, in that `
// ── leg (f) — M6: the rig's arm, the index line, and the script still a script ──
test('(f) [M6] the stub\'s arm answers on its own name and logs every payload', async () => {
`(f) [M6] the arm says \`curl typesafe\` once per request — the \`say\` line the ordering `
'(f) [M6] no request to the endpoint may reach the `*)` fallthrough — the arm sits before it',
'(f) [M6] and appends the `-d` payload as one line to `typesafe.log`',
test('(f) [M6] the exit knob emits nothing and the answers file picks the reply', async () => {
// The exit knob: the requests were made, and none of them answered.
'(f) [M6] `STUB_TYPESAFE_EXIT` still logs the payload — the request was made and refused',
'(f) [M6] and emits nothing, so no row could have taken an answer from it',
// The answers file and the single-reply knob, and the precedence between
// them: the first line whose needle is a substring of the payload wins, and
// `STUB_TYPESAFE_ANSWER` answers every payload no line matched.
`(f) [M6] one row takes the answers file's reply and the other two take `
`(f) [M6] and the default reply answers no payload when a knob is set\n${ledgerRaw(picked)}`,
test('(f) [M6] the README\'s sandbox-boot list names this sim', () => {
// READ, never grepped through a child: a spawn whose call text carries a
// `test_*.mjs` literal is what `test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs` M4 names as a sim
// running a sibling. The section is the one the Proof's fifth `Run:` slices —
// `## The sandbox boot` up to the next `## `.
const from = readme.findIndex((l) => l.startsWith('## The sandbox boot'))
assert.ok(from >= 0, '(f) [M6] `fleet/tests/README.md` must carry a `## The sandbox boot` section')
let to = readme.findIndex((l, i) => i > from && l.startsWith('## '))
`(f) [M6] that section must name this sim, so the index and the directory agree:\n${section}`,
test('(f) [M6] the edited boot script still parses as bash', () => {
// The one reading of the edited script this exam can make on its own, and the
// one every other boot sim rests on. Lines spliced into a `python3` program
// with an unbalanced quote fail here before they fail there.
const r = spawnSync('bash', ['-n', script], { cwd: ROOT, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 60000, env: ENV })
